title: Which real prospecting instruments can detect which resources, at what resolution and depth — grounding the Resource Intelligence sensor ladder
question: What do the real planetary remote-sensing and in-situ instrument literature and current missions establish about which instrument families (passive orbital imaging and VNIR/SWIR spectroscopy, neutron/gamma spectroscopy, radar/subsurface sounding, targeted active spectroscopy, Raman) can detect, discriminate and constrain which resources — at what spatial resolution, penetration depth and composition/depth uncertainty — so that NOXIA's Resource Intelligence state machine and sensor ladder map information classes and confidence to real capability, and so that long-range orbital Raman from 30–50 km is correctly held as an [H] gate and not canonized as today's capability?
why_now: EXT-ENG-NOXIA-20260911-RESOURCE-INTELLIGENCE is open and asks NOXIA to design an explicit pre-deposit knowledge layer (remote sensing -> anomaly -> candidate -> composition_identified -> sampled -> resource_estimated). It names NASA NIAC 2026 'Interworld Slingshot Resource Surveys' 30–50 km Raman as a feasibility study and warns that orbital Raman must stay [H], not [R]. The Moon workstream has just committed to a real global selenographic map (docs/project-workstreams.md, 'Startentscheidung Mond') with geology/resource layers, and NOXIA-RESOURCE-0001/WORLD-0002 define the deposit/discovery-state model the sensor ladder must feed — so the information classes have to be decided now, before the Moon/Mars/Asteroid map layers are built.
real_world_anchor: Demonstrated detection capability, resolution and depth limits of real planetary prospecting instruments (e.g. CRISM, M3, Diviner, LEND, DAN, Mini-RF, SuperCam, SHERLOC) and the NASA NIAC 2026 'Interworld Slingshot Resource Surveys' 30–50 km orbital Raman feasibility study.
novelty_reason: Not a rephrase of RES-20260828-49AF01DE: that candidate asks which bodies physically contain which resources, with what ore grades and extraction feasibility. This gap asks a different question one layer earlier in the chain — which measurement techniques can detect, discriminate and bound those resources, and with what uncertainty — i.e. the detection/information side rather than the deposit side. It also directly serves an actively open Engineering request whose sensor ladder is marked [H]/feasibility-only.
